# Multi-Robot & Fleet Orchestration

> Coordinating multiple robots, fleets and human-robot teams with language-model agents.  
> Layer: L4 · 46 entries · [overview](../README.md#multi-agent) · [survey](../SURVEY.md)

**Legend:** 🟢 open · 🟡 partial · 🔵 api · ⚪ closed. Hover a name for the full paper title. Newest first within each year.

**2026**

- ⚪ [**DuoMind**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02161 "DuoMind: Enabling Distributed Multi-Robot Coordination with Semantic Communication") · 2026-10 — Distributed hierarchical multi-robot framework: each robot pairs a VLM orchestrator, which reasons over its observations and peer messages, with a VLA executor, and robots coordinate through semantic messages; introduces the RoboPoly long-horizon coordination benchmark.
- ⚪ [**RoboTalk**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23997 "RoboTalk: Learning Multi-Robot Communication and Coordination from Multimodal Demonstrations") · 2026-09 · UMass Amherst et al. — Synthetic data pipeline and dataset of 7,950 multimodal trajectories over 53 kitchen mobile-manipulation tasks, with leader-follower planning, tool calls, rationales and natural-language messages, for training small on-device VLMs to communicate and coordinate. _Note: First-party result of 77% success on held-out tasks after fine-tuning vs ~2% untuned; dataset release not verified._
- ⚪ [**Robion**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12075 "Efficient Vision-Language-Action Management and Serving for Robot Factories") · 2026-09 · Max Planck Institute for Software Systems — Serving and management system for fleet-scale VLA inference on multi-GPU edge servers under latency SLOs, co-scheduling VLM and action-diffusion stages on one GPU and placing multiple models; reports up to 64 robots served from a 4-GPU server (first-party).
- ⚪ [**ORCH**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11737 "Organizational Principles Enable Collective Intelligence in Embodied AI") · 2026-09 · Duke University — Builds task-specific hierarchies of LLM-driven embodied agents from organization theory (pooled vs. sequential interdependence); on 25 wildfire-response missions with up to 50 heterogeneous agents it beat four prior multi-agent frameworks (first-party). [project](https://generalroboticslab.com/ORCH)
- ⚪ [**COMPASS**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28247 "Controlling Collectives of AI Agents in Reasoning Space with Spatial Transformers") · 2026-09 — Decentralized architecture for large collectives of LLM-driven robots: on each robot a spatial transformer aggregates multi-hop messages into a learned feedback token for reasoning-space feedback control; commands flocks of up to 1,024 simulated drones in natural language.
- 🟢 [**AeroWeaver**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18520 "AeroWeaver: An Embodied-Agent Harness for Weaving Aerial Skills into Distributed, Adaptive Swarm Execution") · 2026-09 · Beihang University — Embodied-agent harness for UAV swarms that connects LLM decisions to governed skills, runs role-conditioned local agents for distributed coordination without a central joint-action agent, and refines skill selection from role-indexed experience. [code](https://github.com/Admire-ljb/AeroWeaver) · [project](https://admire-ljb.github.io/AeroWeaver/)
- ⚪ [**Physical Agentic AI**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22657 "Physical Agentic AI: An Architecture for Orchestrating a Robot Crew with LLMs") · 2026-08 — Non-actuating LLM mission planner assigns phases to typed robot skills while a deterministic orchestrator validates each dispatch against capabilities, state and workflow contracts before motion (drone, UGV, G1, Go2).
- ⚪ [**EFLUX**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12050 "EFLUX: Elastic Multi-Robot Formation Navigation and Adaptation with Agentic LLMs") · 2026-07 · University of Pennsylvania, University of Southern California — Geometry-grounded LLM agent for multi-robot formation navigation that reasons jointly over deformation (scaling, shearing) and reconfiguration (split, merge) and turns strategies into per-robot waypoints via a generate-verify-correct loop; sim and hardware tests.
- ⚪ [**D-VLC**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29009 "D-VLC: Decentralized Vision-Language Collaboration for Heterogeneous Embodied Multi-Robot Systems in Unknown Environments") · 2026-07 · Zhejiang University et al. — Decentralized, asynchronous VLM collaboration for heterogeneous robot teams in unknown environments, combining lightweight information sharing, capability-aware collaboration and a unified action interface so general VLMs emit actions run by learning-free experts.
- ⚪ [**Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06990 "A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Robust Multi-Robot Manipulation") · 2026-07 · Sun Yat-sen University — Hierarchical LLM agents for multi-robot manipulation: a Planning Agent allocates sub-tasks, per-robot Manipulation Agents act through adaptive tool use, and a Verification Agent monitors physical outcomes and feeds back semantic corrections. Real-robot tests; RSS 2026.
- ⚪ [**DynaHMRC**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14882 "DynaHMRC: Decentralized Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Collaboration for Dynamic Tasks with Large Language Models") · 2026-06 · University of Science and Technology of China, University of Macau — Each robot is a role-aware LLM agent; the team collaborates through self-description, leadership bidding for task allocation, leader election and reflective execution. Adds a benchmark of dynamic task variants and fine-tunes domain-specific LLMs.
- 🟢 [**ROSClaw**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04664 "ROSClaw: A Hierarchical Semantic-Physical Framework for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Collaboration") · 2026-04 · Tongji University — Agent framework for heterogeneous robots with one VLM controller that uses e-URDF descriptions as physical constraints, maps simulated and real agents, logs execution data for iterative policy improvement, and hands task-specific control to different robots. _Note: The repo presents it as a "physical AI runtime for embodied agents"; could also fit framework._ [code](https://github.com/ros-claw/rosclaw) · [project](https://www.rosclaw.io/)
- 🟢 [**Scale-Plan**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08814 "Scale-Plan: Scalable Language-Enabled Task Planning for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Teams") · 2026-03 · Honda Research Institute — Given a PDDL domain, builds an action graph and uses shallow LLM reasoning to extract a compact, task-relevant problem from object-rich scenes before planning, to curb hallucination and weak grounding in heterogeneous multi-robot teams; evaluated in AI2-THOR. IROS 2026. [code](https://github.com/honda-research-institute/Scale_Plan)
- ⚪ [**IndoorR2X**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20182 "IndoorR2X: Indoor Robot-to-Everything Coordination with LLM-Driven Planning") · 2026-03 · Fujitsu Research, Carnegie Mellon University — Benchmark and simulation framework for LLM-driven multi-robot task planning that fuses observations from mobile robots and static IoT sensors (e.g., cameras) into a global semantic state, reducing redundant exploration. _Note: Code release not verified._ [project](https://fandulu.github.io/IndoorR2X_project_page/)
- ⚪ [**IMR-LLM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02669 "IMR-LLM: Industrial Multi-Robot Task Planning and Program Generation using Large Language Models") · 2026-03 · Shenzhen University et al. — Industrial multi-robot planning: LLMs help build disjunctive graphs that are solved deterministically for a feasible high-level plan, and a process tree guides LLMs to generate executable low-level robot programs; introduces the three-level IMR-Bench.
- ⚪ [**AgentComm-Bench**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20285 "AgentComm-Bench: Stress-Testing Cooperative Embodied AI Under Latency, Packet Loss, and Bandwidth Collapse") · 2026-03 — Stress-tests cooperative embodied AI under six communication impairments (latency, packet loss, bandwidth collapse, asynchronous updates, stale memory, conflicting evidence) across cooperative perception, multi-agent navigation and zone search. _Note: No code link found._
- ⚪ [**KGLAMP**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04129 "KGLAMP: Knowledge Graph-guided Language model for Adaptive Multi-robot Planning and Replanning") · 2026-02 · Honda Research Institute USA, University of Maryland — A knowledge graph of object relations, spatial reachability and robot capabilities guides an LLM to write PDDL problems for heterogeneous teams, serves as persistent memory updated with observations, and triggers replanning on inconsistencies; tested on MAT-THOR.
- 🟢 [**CommCP**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06038 "CommCP: Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination via LLM-Based Communication with Conformal Prediction") · 2026-02 · UC Riverside — Decentralized LLM communication for heterogeneous robots on multi-agent multi-task embodied question answering; conformal prediction calibrates generated messages to limit receiver distraction. Ships an MM-EQA benchmark. ICRA 2026. [code](https://github.com/tasl-lab/CommCP) · [project](https://comm-cp.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**MeCo**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20577 "MeCo: Enhancing LLM-Empowered Multi-Robot Collaboration via Similar Task Memoization") · 2026-01 · Northwestern Polytechnical University et al. — Memoization for LLM-driven multi-robot collaboration: a similarity test retrieves previously solved, similar tasks so their plans can be reused without re-invoking the LLM; introduces MeCoBench for similar-task scenarios. AAMAS 2026. [code](https://github.com/TomWang-NPU/MeCo)
- ⚪ [**EmboTeam**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.11063 "EmboTeam: Grounding LLM Reasoning into Reactive Behavior Trees via PDDL for Embodied Multi-Robot Collaboration") · 2026-01 · Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences — Three-stage planner for heterogeneous teams: an LLM writes PDDL problems, a classical planner searches for action sequences, and plans compile into behavior trees for reactive control with a shared blackboard; introduces the MACE-THOR benchmark (42 tasks). _Note: First-party comparison reports gains over LaMMA-P on MACE-THOR._

**2025**

- ⚪ [**InteractGen**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00797 "Transforming Monolithic Foundation Models into Embodied Multi-Agent Architectures for Human-Robot Collaboration") · 2025-11 · Tsinghua University et al. — LLM-powered multi-agent framework that splits robot intelligence into agents for perception, dependency-aware planning, decision and verification, failure reflection and dynamic delegation to humans; reported in a three-month shared-office deployment (first-party).
- 🟢 [**RobotFleet**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10379 "RobotFleet: An Open-Source Framework for Centralized Multi-Robot Task Planning") · 2025-10 · University of Southern California — Open-source framework for centralized LLM-based planning and scheduling across heterogeneous robot fleets; robots run as containerized services, with a shared declarative world state and two-way communication for execution and replanning. [code](https://github.com/therohangupta/robot-fleet)
- 🟡 [**RoboOS-NeXT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26536 "RoboOS-NeXT: A Unified Memory-based Framework for Lifelong, Scalable, and Robust Multi-Robot Collaboration") · 2025-10 · BAAI, Peking University — Extends RoboOS with a Spatio-Temporal-Embodiment Memory (STEM) that fuses scene geometry, event history and embodiment profiles into one shared representation inside a brain-cerebellum framework, for lifelong, scalable and failure-robust multi-robot collaboration. _Note: RoboOS code is open; a NeXT-specific code release was not verified._ [project](https://flagopen.github.io/RoboOS/)
- ⚪ [**PIP-LLM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22784 "PIP-LLM: Integrating PDDL-Integer Programming with LLMs for Coordinating Multi-Robot Teams Using Natural Language") · 2025-10 · University of Southern California, University of Pennsylvania — Translates a command into a team-level PDDL problem, turns the resulting plan into a subtask dependency graph, then solves integer programs to allocate subtasks to robots, optimizing travel cost and workload under capability and user constraints.
- ⚪ [**FLEET**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07417 "FLEET: Formal Language-Grounded Scheduling for Heterogeneous Robot Teams") · 2025-10 · Johns Hopkins University APL, DEVCOM ARL — An LLM front-end outputs a task graph with durations and precedence plus a capability-aware robot-task fitness matrix; a MILP back-end minimizes makespan while robots run subtasks with agentic closed-loop control. Hardware trials use two quadrupeds.
- ⚪ [**Prompting Robot Teams**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.24575 "Prompting Robot Teams with Natural Language") · 2025-09 · University of Cambridge — Distills an LLM's task decomposition into a small RNN whose states track a task automaton, plus a GNN policy conditioned on those states and language embeddings, so robot teams run language-specified tasks decentrally without calling the LLM at runtime. RA-L. [project](https://sites.google.com/view/prompting-teams)
- 🟢 [**DEXTER-LLM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14387 "DEXTER-LLM: Dynamic and Explainable Coordination of Multi-Robot Systems in Unknown Environments via Large Language Models") · 2025-08 · Peking University, Duke Kunshan University — Online multi-robot coordination in unknown environments: parses missions in natural language or LTL, generates subtasks with multi-stage LLM reasoning, assigns them by search-based optimization, and updates plans with human-in-the-loop verification as new tasks appear. [code](https://github.com/TCXM/DEXTER-LLM) · [project](https://tcxm.github.io/DEXTER-LLM/)
- ⚪ [**LAN2CB**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16068 "Compositional Coordination for Multi-Robot Teams with Large Language Models") · 2025-07 · University of Southern California, University of Pennsylvania — Converts natural-language mission descriptions into executable Python for multi-robot teams by parsing missions into behavior trees and generating control code from them plus a structured knowledge base; adds a mission-description dataset. MRS 2025 oral. _Note: Evaluated in simulation and on real robots (first-party); code release not verified._ [project](https://sites.google.com/view/lan-cb)
- 🟢 [**VIKI-R**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09049 "VIKI-R: Coordinating Embodied Multi-Agent Cooperation via Reinforcement Learning") · 2025-06 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai AI Laboratory et al. — VIKI-Bench tests embodied multi-agent cooperation at three levels (agent activation, task planning, trajectory perception) across robot morphologies; VIKI-R fine-tunes a VLM on chain-of-thought demonstrations, then with multi-level RL rewards. NeurIPS 2025 D&B. [code](https://github.com/MARS-EAI/VIKI-R) · [project](https://faceong.github.io/VIKI-R/)
- ⚪ [**Multi-Robot 3D Scene Graph Planning**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07454 "Language-Grounded Hierarchical Planning and Execution with Multi-Robot 3D Scene Graphs") · 2025-06 · MIT, DEVCOM Army Research Laboratory — Fuses robots' open-set object maps into a shared 3D scene graph used for relocalization and task and motion planning, while an LLM turns operator intent into PDDL goals using scene-graph and robot capability context; tested on large-scale outdoor tasks. [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8xbGGOLfLAY)
- 🟢 [**RoboOS**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03673 "RoboOS: A Hierarchical Embodied Framework for Cross-Embodiment and Multi-Agent Collaboration") · 2025-05 · BAAI, Peking University — Open-source brain-cerebellum system for multi-robot collaboration: the RoboBrain MLLM plans, a plug-and-play cerebellum skill library executes, and real-time shared memory syncs multi-agent state; the repo's 2.0 version adds a SaaS + MCP structure. _Note: Could also be listed under harness; placed here because multi-agent collaboration is its headline contribution._ [code](https://github.com/FlagOpen/RoboOS) · [project](https://flagopen.github.io/RoboOS/)
- ⚪ [**HMCF**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00820 "HMCF: A Human-in-the-loop Multi-Robot Collaboration Framework Based on Large Language Models") · 2025-05 · University of Southampton — Human-in-the-loop multi-robot framework: every heterogeneous robot has an LLM agent that reasons about its own capabilities for task allocation and execution, while a human operator oversees the team and intervenes only when needed.
- 🟢 [**GenSwarm**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.23875 "GenSwarm: Scalable Multi-Robot Code-Policy Generation and Deployment via Language Models") · 2025-03 · Westlake University et al. — End-to-end multi-language-agent system that turns natural-language instructions into white-box code policies for multi-robot tasks and deploys them on simulated and real robot swarms. Published in npj Robotics. [code](https://github.com/WindyLab/GenSwarm)

**2024**

- 🟢 [**SwarmGPT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.08428 "SwarmGPT: Combining Large Language Models with Safe Motion Planning for Drone Swarm Choreography") · 2024-12 · Technical University of Munich — Language-based choreographer for drone swarms: an LLM designs performances and a safety filter minimally corrects plans that violate safety or feasibility constraints; shown in simulation with up to 200 drones and on hardware with up to 20. RA-L 2025. [code](https://github.com/utiasDSL/swarmGPT) · [project](https://utiasdsl.github.io/swarm_GPT/)
- 🟢 [**DART-LLM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.09022 "DART-LLM: Dependency-Aware Multi-Robot Task Decomposition and Execution using Large Language Models") · 2024-11 · The University of Tokyo — Decomposes natural-language instructions into subtasks linked by a directed acyclic graph of dependencies, assigns them to robots, executes them through an actuation module and perceives the scene with a VLM-based object detector. _Note: Code is split across several module repositories linked from the project page._ [code](https://github.com/wyd0817/DART_LLM_Task_Decomposer_Module) · [project](https://wyd0817.github.io/project-dart-llm/)
- 🟢 [**LLM2Swarm**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11387 "LLM2Swarm: Robot Swarms that Responsively Reason, Plan, and Collaborate through LLMs") · 2024-10 · IRIDIA (Universite Libre de Bruxelles), CISPA — Proof-of-concept integration of LLMs with robot swarms in two modes: indirect (LLMs synthesize and validate controllers) and direct (each robot runs its own LLM for robot-robot and human-swarm dialogue, e.g., to detect anomalies). NeurIPS 2024 workshop. [code](https://github.com/Pold87/LLM2Swarm)
- 🟢 [**EMOS**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22662 "EMOS: Embodiment-aware Heterogeneous Multi-robot Operating System with LLM Agents") · 2024-10 · National University of Singapore et al. — LLM multi-agent system for heterogeneous robots in which each agent writes its own "robot resume" by reading its URDF and calling kinematics tools, instead of human-assigned roles, before planning and task allocation; introduces the Habitat-MAS benchmark. _Note: The repo describes itself as an early release._ [code](https://github.com/SgtVincent/EMOS)
- 🟢 [**LaMMA-P**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.20560 "LaMMA-P: Generalizable Multi-Agent Long-Horizon Task Allocation and Planning with LM-Driven PDDL Planner") · 2024-09 · UC Riverside — Couples LM reasoning with a classical heuristic-search PDDL planner to identify and allocate subtasks across heterogeneous robot teams on long-horizon tasks; introduces the MAT-THOR benchmark in AI2-THOR. ICRA 2025. [code](https://github.com/tasl-lab/LaMMA-P) · [project](https://lamma-p.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**COHERENT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15146 "COHERENT: Collaboration of Heterogeneous Multi-Robot System with Large Language Models") · 2024-09 · Shanghai AI Laboratory, Northwestern Polytechnical University — LLM task planning for heterogeneous teams (quadrotors, robot dogs, arms) via a Proposal-Execution-Feedback-Adjustment loop: a central assigner decomposes and assigns subtasks, each robot executor picks a feasible action and reports feedback for adjustment. ICRA 2025. [code](https://github.com/MrKeee/COHERENT)
- 🟢 [**LLaMAR**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10031 "LLaMAR: Long-Horizon Planning for Multi-Agent Robots in Partially Observable Environments") · 2024-07 · MIT et al. — LM-based cognitive architecture for long-horizon multi-agent planning under partial observability, using a plan-act-correct-verify loop that self-corrects from execution feedback without oracles or simulators; introduces the MAP-THOR suite in AI2-THOR. [code](https://github.com/nsidn98/LLaMAR)
- ⚪ [**AutoRT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12963 "AutoRT: Embodied Foundation Models for Large Scale Orchestration of Robotic Agents") · 2024-01 · Google DeepMind — Fleet orchestration for data collection: a VLM describes each robot's scene, an LLM proposes diverse tasks, and a prompt-level "robot constitution" of safety rules filters them. DeepMind reports up to 20 robots at once and 77,000 trials over seven months (first-party). _Note: All deployed robots were under human supervision per the DeepMind blog._ [project](https://auto-rt.github.io/) · [blog](https://deepmind.google/blog/shaping-the-future-of-advanced-robotics/)

**2023**

- 🟢 [**Co-NavGPT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.07937 "Co-NavGPT: Multi-Robot Cooperative Visual Semantic Navigation Using Vision Language Models") · 2023-10 · University of Groningen — A VLM acts as global planner for multi-robot visual target navigation: sub-maps from several robots are merged into one global map encoding robot states and frontiers, and the VLM assigns frontiers to robots. Evaluated on HM3D scenes. [code](https://github.com/ybgdgh/Co-NavGPT) · [project](https://sites.google.com/view/co-navgpt2)
- 🟢 [**SMART-LLM**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10062 "SMART-LLM: Smart Multi-Agent Robot Task Planning using Large Language Models") · 2023-09 · Purdue University — Few-shot programmatic LLM prompting pipeline that turns a high-level instruction into a multi-robot plan via task decomposition, coalition formation and task allocation; ships a benchmark of instructions of varying complexity and is tested in simulation and on real robots. [code](https://github.com/SMARTlab-Purdue/SMART-LLM) · [project](https://sites.google.com/view/smart-llm/)
- 🟢 [**HMAS-2 (Scalable Multi-Robot Collaboration)**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15943 "Scalable Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models: Centralized or Decentralized Systems?") · 2023-09 · MIT — Compares centralized, decentralized and two hybrid LLM communication frameworks for multi-robot planning on success rate and token efficiency; a hybrid design (HMAS-2) scaled best as agent count grew and was also shown in 3D simulation. [code](https://github.com/yongchao98/multi-agent-framework) · [project](https://yongchao98.github.io/MIT-REALM-Multi-Robot/)
- 🟢 [**RoCo**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04738 "RoCo: Dialectic Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models") · 2023-07 · Columbia University — Each robot arm is driven by an LLM agent; agents discuss strategy in dialogue, propose sub-task plans and task-space waypoints for a multi-arm motion planner, and revise them in-context from environment feedback such as collision checks. Introduces RoCoBench. [code](https://github.com/MandiZhao/robot-collab) · [project](https://project-roco.github.io/)
- 🟢 [**CoELA**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.02485 "Building Cooperative Embodied Agents Modularly with Large Language Models") · 2023-07 · UMass Amherst et al. — Cooperative Embodied Language Agent: a modular LLM agent (perception, memory, communication, planning, execution) for decentralized multi-agent cooperation with costly communication, evaluated on C-WAH and TDW-MAT. ICLR 2024. _Note: First-party result that GPT-4-driven CoELA beat planning-based baselines; open LLMs lagged._ [code](https://github.com/UMass-Foundation-Model/Co-LLM-Agents) · [project](https://umass-embodied-agi.github.io/CoELA/)
